title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference | Week 11 vs. Kansas City Chiefs
headline: Hjalte Froholdt is still in concussion protocol with a decision likely tomorrow. Rookie QB Carson Beck keeps the job, and Kansas City is expected to bracket Trey McBride in spots.
summary: LaFleur opened with injuries. Jon Gaines will be limited and is trending well. He gave no update on a player he called "James" (the question's caption spelling was "James Connor") beyond saying the player is working hard to return and that it was not a good injury. Center Hjalte Froholdt ("Fro") has not cleared concussion protocol. Wednesday is the non-contact stage, and the team will know more tomorrow. LaFleur said Froholdt could help rookie QB Carson Beck, who got his first walkthrough reps with him in the huddle. LaFleur praised Beck's composure and approach and said he is evaluated week to week. For Kansas City he expects a tough, old-school defense under Spagnuolo that will bracket Trey McBride situationally, which should free other pass catchers. LaFleur likes the play style of corner Kei'Trel Clark, who started last week, and hopes the three corners play well. He was very positive on Elijah Higgins after his extension, calling him an elite blocker who could grow more with the ball.

title: Jesse Minter on Rebounding From a Loss
headline: Ravens activate RB Adam Randall off IR and he is available this week, while DT Nnamdi Madubuike's hamstring is a wait-and-see issue after missing practice.
summary: Minter opened by saying it is a short week after the Monday night game. The team spent the day evaluating film and having tough, honest conversations. Baltimore activated Randall from IR, so he is on the 53-man roster and available this week. Asked about the five-game losing streak, Minter said morale is really about telling the truth, focusing on improvement and building processes that lead to performance. He said his blunt style isn't new, it is just more visible now that he is head coach. On Nnamdi Madubuike, he said the hamstring would have kept him out of practice today and that the team will check his response toward the end of the week before judging his availability. He declined to discuss Marlon Humphrey's podcast comments about Baltimore, saying such conversations stay private, and spoke warmly about the city. No opponent or game-plan details were given.

Dealing with a hamstring and would not have practiced today. The team will see how it responds toward the end of the week before deciding his availability for the game.

signals.claim: Madubuike's availability for this week's game will be decided toward the end of the week based on how his hamstring responds.
signals.note: A hamstring issue that kept him out of the first practice puts his Week availability in doubt, which matters for IDP and defensive-line depth.
signals.quote: He would have not practiced today.

topics.detail: Minter framed morale as honesty about where the team stands, focusing on improvement and building processes that lead to performance. He said the veterans don't lack individual confidence.
He said he has always been blunt about performance and that it is just more visible now as head coach. The approach is to learn from each day and keep improving.
Minter said conversations like that stay private within the building. He emphasized his pride in the city of Baltimore and his desire to represent it well by how the team plays.
Randall was activated from IR and is available this week, which adds RB depth. Minter gave no specifics on his role.

title: Joe Brady On The Return Of Tyrell Shavers, Preparing For the Dolphins, And More
headline: Christian Benford's status is unresolved after he left last week's game, with Maxwell Hairston ready to step in. WR Tyrell Shavers joins the 53-man roster, but his game-day status is undecided.
summary: Brady was asked about Christian Benford, who has been banged up repeatedly. He called it a concern but promised a better answer at the end of the week, and said the depth behind Benford is trusted. Maxwell Hairston got high marks for handling the corner spot after Benford went down last week. Tyrell Shavers is being added to the 53-man roster, but Brady wouldn't say whether he will be active on game day. Brady said rookie T.J. Parker played his best football last week, but he downplayed snap counts and said edge rotation depends on the opponent's personnel and drive length. He praised Skyler Bell's attitude despite no catches in three games and compared it to Carlisle's rookie year. He also said Ed Oliver and Bradley Chubb are disrupting even without sacks, because opponents slide protection and chip them. Brady said he hesitates to let Josh Allen run QB sneaks or keepers near the goal line because of the hits, and he credited James for a short-yardage conversion last week. For Sunday at Miami, he called the Dolphins well coached and young, with Kyle McCord having more experience now, and said Chop Robinson will be a huge focus. He added that the Thursday turnaround next week doesn't change this week's approach.

Brady hasn't seen a rookie wall and said the staff communicates with the rookies regularly about their roles. He also said Khalil Shakir's perimeter blocking from last week is going on teach tape.

title: Dave Canales: 'We gotta go back to work'
headline: Bryce Young's foot soreness is gone and he practiced with no restrictions, but TEs Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller are day-to-day. Jonathon Brooks and Michael Jackson are ready to return pending roster moves.
summary: Canales opened by preaching "Work Wednesday" and the focus on a home game against the Ravens while Carolina leads the division. He said Jonathon Brooks, Michael Jackson and Brady Christensen are physically ready, but the team has to work through roster space and the open practice windows before activating them. Bryce Young got sore after the Packers game, felt better each day, and moved around and sprinted with no restrictions on Wednesday. The tight end room is a real concern: Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller were not out there, the team has a practice-squad tight end filling reps, and the staff will decide after Thursday's work whether they can go. Canales is managing Chuba Hubbard's practice reps so he can carry the Sunday load, and he wants Xavier Legette to play more after only two snaps in his first game back from IR. He said Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker are important this week and need to get back into rhythm. Jaelan Phillips was praised for his Defensive Player of the Week performance and the way he creates pass-rush opportunities for others, while Tyrel Dodson was praised for filling in for Bobby Okereke, whose foot injury is being taken day to day without an IR move.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “Christian Parker Is a Huge Part of the Solution” | Press Conference
headline: Mike Pettine takes over Cowboys defensive play-calling for the rest of the year (Christian Parker stays DC); expect personnel rotation changes and a Javonte Williams touch emphasis vs. the Titans.
summary: Schottenheimer announced that senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will call defensive plays starting Sunday, and he plans for that to last the whole season. Christian Parker remains defensive coordinator, still running meetings and walkthroughs, but no longer calls plays on game day. The coach pointed to game-day inconsistency over the past few weeks and said a different perspective was needed. He described the decision as collaborative, made Tuesday mid-morning after talks with Parker starting Monday, with front office alignment from Jerry and Stephen Jones. Schottenheimer said Pettine is big on pressuring the quarterback and unsettling the offense, and that he looks at personnel differently. He said the team is also adjusting personnel rotations on defense, playing some guys more and others less, but named no one. On offense, he said Javonte Williams gets stronger as games go on and needs touches to find rhythm. He named tackling, communication, and ball security as the three areas where the team must do the simple things better. He called the Titans game and the following one very important for a 4-6 team with seven games left.

signals.claim: Williams will be prioritized for more touches to get into a rhythm, as the run game depends on his attempts.
signals.note: The coach tied run-game success to Williams' volume and called him a bruising back who improves with touches, which supports a heavy workload.
signals.quote: getting him the touches that he needs to find his rhythm

topics.detail: Mike Pettine will call defensive plays on Sundays for the rest of the season. Christian Parker remains DC and keeps running meetings and walkthroughs. It is not yet decided whether Pettine will call from the field or the box.

Communication overall, ball security on offense, and tackling on defense. Thursday practice is in pads with more tackling work, likely the last padded practice for a while because of the short weeks ahead.
Schottenheimer says he likes to get players involved and wants to get Dak Prescott off to a good start, with CeeDee Lamb getting touches.
At 4-6 with seven games left, he said missing the playoffs would make the season a failure and called the next two games very important.

title: HC Sean Payton on continuing to chase improvement: ‘There’s a lot that still needs to be done’
headline: Payton gave no specific Broncos player news. The bye helped some banged-up players, and he refused to discuss OL, RB or lineup changes before facing the Raiders.
summary: Payton said the first full Wednesday practice after the bye went well and was longer than the one two weeks earlier. He said a handful of players who could not have played last Sunday have a chance to play this Sunday, but he named no one. He declined to discuss lineups, the offensive line, the running backs or depth, only saying the team will get better in those areas. He added that he feels good about both the starters and the depth. He described the Broncos as a little more than halfway through the season with a lot still to be done, and said they need to block cleaner after missed chances against Carolina. On the Raiders, he praised Klint Kubiak's system and expects a strong run game with play-action and boot concepts. He noted the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins and that the Broncos had a week of tape on the new rookie quarterback, Fernando Mendoza. He credited the Raiders' defense with varied fronts and nickel looks that look simple but are hard to block. He also said he watched Seattle and other games on the bye, and that self-scouting is easier now that information is updated weekly.

injuries.detail: Payton said a handful of players who would have missed last Sunday's game have a chance to play this Sunday, but he named none. He also said a player who worked hard since May had his first practice today after a setback. The captions garble the name, so it is unclear who he meant.

topics.detail: Payton expects Kubiak's scheme to feature the run game and play-action boot concepts, with Mendoza starting at quarterback after the Cousins trade. He said the Broncos got a week of tape on Mendoza, praising his quick release and winner's profile.
He said the Raiders show a variety of fronts and nickel packages, with some players moving between the back end and the front. These looks are complicated to block even when they appear simple.

Payton said the team feels good about its starters and depth, and he declined to discuss lineups or changes on the offensive line or at running back. He acknowledged that mid-season line changes can be challenging and said the team needs to block cleaner, citing missed opportunities against Carolina.

Asked about a receiver winning at the line on a touchdown against Carolina, Payton called it a strength thanks to his size and hand use. The name is unclear in the captions. He said he likes bigger receivers because the target radius is quarterback friendly.

Payton said the full bye week helps players recover mentally and physically, and that injured players are around the team. Since information now updates weekly, self-scouting no longer depends on the bye week, though the staff keeps doing it.

He expects a run-heavy offense led by Bucky Irving, with Rachaad White-type depth from Gainwell, and said Detroit also wants to establish the run. Campbell did not confirm that, but said he feels good about the edge group and that Skyler Gill-Howard's versatility makes some edge work 'a possibility'. He also highlighted Tyler Lacy as a big, stout player who can work on the edge. A player who has been a healthy scratch all year (the name is garbled in the captions) is going to be 'gotten going' soon. Campbell described a standout player, likely Jahmyr Gibbs, as gaining strength through the season after arriving in great shape. He closed by crediting the home crowd for Detroit's unbeaten record at Ford Field.

title: Liam Coen on Prep for Giants, Offensive Challenges & Communication Being Key | Press Conference
headline: Jonah Monheim starts on the Jaguars' offensive line in place of Robert Hainsey (concussion), and the Jaguars are still pushing for a better run game after a 26-carry game from their lead back.
summary: Coen praised the Giants as a tough, physical team under Harbaugh. He singled out Isaiah Likely, the quarterback getting more comfortable in the system, and an offense that can go heavy or spread teams out. He said the game will be decided in the trenches, with a lot of New York pressure, fire zones and zero blitzes. That makes communication on the offensive line, and from the backs and tight ends, a priority, and it will be tested on the road with a silent cadence. He confirmed Robert Hainsey is out, so Jonah Monheim will play. Monheim has taken a lot of practice reps while Hainsey was limited and came in to help close out last week's game. Coen was pleased with the 36-run, 35-pass balance and the touchdown drive that closed the game, but wants more consistent 5-8 yard runs from better blocking and better vision from the backs. He said yards per carry can be misleading and that he judges the run game by whether it sets up play action. He was impressed by the toughness of the back who carried 26 times last week while not fully healthy. He also said the two new additions, including safety Jesse Bates, were held out of last week's game to learn, and will be integrated this week with Antonio Johnson and the other veteran defensive backs helping out.

title: Andy Reid on Week 10 Matchup | Press Conference 11/18
headline: Kenneth Walker III (groin) sat out Wednesday and is day-to-day, Trey Smith is in the concussion protocol, and Josh Downs may see more work this week.
summary: Reid opened by saying Jaylon Moore is making progress, Trey Smith is in the concussion protocol, and Kenneth Walker III did not practice. He called Walker's groin a day-to-day issue that is improving but still bothers him, and said the team is being careful. The Chiefs face Arizona, whom Reid called a well-coached team under a first-year head coach, with tight systems. Reid said Patrick Mahomes looks the same as before, with strong legs, and is staying in the pocket while still moving when needed. Travis Kelce's high ankle sprain was a quick tweak early in the game, so Reid held him back, and Kelce is now running around. Newly acquired Josh Downs has impressed as a smart player who picked up most of the game plan and the two-minute offense, and he is a good route runner with secure hands. Reid said Downs might get a little more work this week, and that Mahomes will throw to whoever is open. Reid also praised the trust Mahomes showed in a receiver coming off a hamstring injury and in Andrew Armstrong on downfield shots. He addressed Matt Prater's tryout by saying general manager Veach is simply bringing in kickers to cover the bases.

title: Head Coach Kevin O'Connell on Preparing for the 49ers, Injury Updates & Offensive Performance
headline: Jordan Addison had successful thumb surgery and, for now, won't go on short-term IR, so O'Connell is hopeful he plays vs. the 49ers; Blake Cashman is likely back Sunday, while T.J. Hockenson and Kyler Murray remain out.
summary: O'Connell called the Week 11 Mexico City game against the 49ers a significant challenge. Asked about confidence in Frank, Glenn said he has a lot of confidence in him. The question came after a defensive play-calling change last week.
Glenn rejected the idea that the team, at 2-8, would be better off losing for draft position.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: November 18, 2026
headline: Eagles keep Sean as offensive play caller after the bye, with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks hopeful but unconfirmed for Sunday against the Steelers; Makai Lemon's role is expected to grow.
summary: Sirianni said the team will miss Jordan Davis after trading him, but he feels good about the defensive tackle depth and the return the team got. He gave no firm answer at nose tackle, saying practice this week will tell a lot and that the practice squad has some depth. Sean remains the offensive play caller after a bye-week review. Sirianni admitted the offense hasn't been good enough, while saying he likes the plan going forward. He also brought T.J. Paganetti back as an extra set of eyes on the offense, in the way he previously used Marcus Brady. Joe Milton III was asked about starting Sunday and Sirianni said he'll be in there, then praised his work ethic. DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are not ruled in or out: he feels pretty good but promised nothing and will watch practice. He was upbeat on Makai Lemon, saying he has been productive this past month and that more can be added to his plate. He said tight end Eli Stowers is developing and can earn more reps through special teams. His message to the team was that competitors compete, that there is still hope in the division, and that this is a chance to grow. He also praised Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers.

title: Shanahan, McCaffrey Talk Colorado Prep, Preview Tough Defense
headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) sat out Wednesday's practice but Shanahan is hopeful he returns tomorrow; Keenan Allen is expected to be in the plan every week.
summary: Shanahan opened with the injury report. Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice but Shanahan hopes he can go tomorrow, taking it day by day. Dre Greenlaw and Nick Bosa also appear to have sat out, though the captions are garbled. Several players were limited: Renardo Green (back), Upton Stout (shoulder and neck), Siran Neal (knee and foot), and Ji'Ayir Brown (ankle). Most of the session was about preparing for Brian Flores' Vikings defense, which Shanahan says blitzes more than anyone and creates pressure on every one of its roughly 70 plays. He said the offense's job is to avoid negative plays, especially turnovers and lost yardage, while staying aggressive. He praised Brock Purdy as a steady, even-keeled quarterback whose game plan doesn't change with who is available. He expects Keenan Allen to be part of the plan every week and is confident Jacob Cowing can be a good punt returner. Shanahan also covered altitude acclimation in Colorado, the benefits of a road week, and the team's depth culture. He said Kirk Cousins looked like his usual self for Minnesota and that the earlier meeting with him matters little.

title: Todd Bowles on Baker Mayfield’s Outlook | Press Conference
headline: Baker Mayfield's foot injury leaves his Week 11 status open until Friday, and Antoine Winfield Jr. is also sore. Jalon Daniels is the likely fill-in at QB, with Cooper Rush signed as depth.
summary: Bowles said Baker Mayfield did not practice Wednesday because of a foot injury on the side or inside of the foot. He called Mayfield much better than a week ago but would not say whether he is ready, and the decision will come Friday after Bowles sees him work. Bowles would not say which play caused the injury, and said it was unrelated to Mayfield's thumb. If Mayfield can't play, the offense stays the same apart from 2-3 plays tailored to each QB. The team signed Cooper Rush and elevated another QB for depth. Bowles believes the backup, who has seen the field a few times this year, is better prepared and calmer now. Antoine Winfield Jr. is still pretty sore from the Bears game and was out of practice, so his Sunday availability depends on Thursday and Friday. Bowles said the run game has improved and the passing game is still catching up, citing drops, penalties, play-calling and the rainy game. He said Ted Hurst III needs to play more after getting a single snap against Chicago. He praised Ifeatu Melifonwu's steady work filling in for Winfield and Josiah Trotter's mental growth at linebacker. The next opponent is the Lions, whom he called talented and physical, with Aidan Hutchinson injured and Alim McNeill and Kerby Joseph (probably) back.
